thread.title: 8 Cozy Games for Better Mental Health
thread.title_full: 8 Cozy Games for Better Mental Health

author: Sofia Alvarez
title: 8 Cozy Games for Better Mental Health
text:
Cozy games offer a welcome escape, proving that digital play can be a potent tool for mental well-being.
These digital havens are more than just a trend; they’re a growing movement focused on relaxation and stress relief.
Cozy games are designed for relaxation, featuring low stress and positive reinforcement. They can lower stress and anxiety, offering a sense of accomplishment and distraction. Research suggests benefits similar to meditation and mindfulness practices. Games like Stardew Valley , Palia, and Wylde Flowers are popular choices. Cozy gaming should not replace professional mental health care. Confession: As someone who typically finds video games anxiety-inducing, stumbling upon “cozy game” recommendations on TikTok felt like a revelation. Creator Cozy K shared a June 2024 TikTok with over 400,000 likes, suggesting these games for days when you’re not feeling your best, physically or mentally. But can these digital escapes truly benefit our mental health? Cozy games, often played on devices like the Nintendo Switch or iPhone, are intentionally crafted to help players relax and unwind. Instead of focusing on competition or high-stakes action, they invite you to explore tranquil worlds, engage in virtual cooking, or care for charming creatures. The appeal is simple: lose yourself in the moment without the pressure of urgency or stress.
The Science Behind the Calm “Cozy games are low-stress, enjoyable, and often wholesome online games that are designed to calm your mind and reduce your stress level,” explains psychologist Vanessa Kennedy, PhD, director of psychology at Driftwood Recovery. “They typically involve soothing colors and aesthetics, positive reinforcement, nature or animals, and community interaction.” These games deliberately minimize elements that trigger stress, such as violence, fear, or intense competition. Research is increasingly supporting the use of video games that promote well-being in both adults and youth, according to Mikal Bailey, DMSc, PA-C, MT(ASCP), CEO of Stillwater Health. Potential benefits include reduced stress and anxiety, safe social interactions, a sense of accomplishment, cognitive stimulation, and a way to cope with failure in a controlled environment.
How Cozy Games Impact Your Brain The appeal of cozy gaming is undeniable, especially as the seasons change. Beyond the feel-good factor, there’s emerging science to back up these positive effects. “These games are designed to help you relax and slow down, perhaps at the end of a busy and rushed day,” Dr. Kennedy notes. Activities like designing interiors, farming, gardening, or interacting with in-game characters can foster creativity, a connection with nature, and nurturing instincts.
“Early research into cozy games suggests that they can have positive mental health benefits on par with meditation and mindfulness practices,” Dr. Kennedy states. A 2021 study involving 80 undergraduate students found that playing a cozy game for 20 minutes led to a reduction in blood pressure and heart rate comparable to a 20-minute meditation session. The mechanisms behind this include:
Meditative elements: Growing virtual gardens, crafting, building, or engaging with soothing music and colors can create a meditative state, allowing the brain to focus without judgment, as Dr. Kennedy explains. Distractibility: For those experiencing high stress or anxiety, cozy games offer a healthy distraction. “We can ‘de-stress’ our nervous systems by entering into gaming environments that provide us a greater sense of control,” says Dr. Bailey. “This allows us to detach from other stressors for a period of time, allowing our fight-or-flight response to lessen.” Sense of accomplishment: Completing small tasks, whether fishing, cooking, or managing a virtual farm, can provide a dopamine boost. This creative expression also taps into childlike wonder and joy, as Dr. Kennedy observes. Social connection: Interacting with other players or non-player characters (NPCs) can cultivate positive emotions, leading to a mood boost and a sense of belonging, Dr. Kennedy adds. Choosing Your Digital Oasis The ideal cozy game for mental health is highly personal. Dr. Kennedy recommends selecting games that enhance your sense of relaxation, creativity, and connection. Crucially, these games should be accessible and feature manageable tasks. “Avoid games with high-pressure elements such as intense competition or group battles, time limits, [or] violence,” she advises. Here are a few highly-regarded cozy games circulating on social media:
Palia : This massively multiplayer online (MMO) game lets you tend to a plot of land, engage in activities like fishing, cooking, and foraging within a scenic landscape. “Although there is hunting as a form of combat, the game is mostly focused on socializing than anything else,” notes TikTok creator adroidirl. Tiny Glade : A medieval-themed city-building game where players construct everything from castles to ruins. Commenters on TikTok describe it as “so relaxing and peaceful.” Sun Haven : This fantasy farming game allows you to build and manage your farm, complete tasks, and explore a medieval town. One TikTok user called it their “comfort cozy game,” praising its magical and relaxing qualities. Roots of Pacha : Set in the Stone Age, this farming game is lauded for its relaxing atmosphere and peaceful soundtrack. Interacting with animals through music and community through dance makes it a particularly charming experience, according to the r/CozyGamers subreddit. Strange Horticulture : A slightly spooky option perfect for autumn, where you manage a local plant store. You’ll identify plants, solve puzzles, and navigate multiple endings. A Redditor recommends taking your time to “really enjoy the characters and the storyline,” calling it “V cozy with excellent spooky vibes” for a rainy day. Wylde Flowers : Embrace cottagecore with this story-driven game where you become a witch. You’ll farm, cast spells, and complete quests. One player appreciates the ability to “change the seasons when you want to, so you’re not rushed for time,” as shared on Reddit. Wytchwood : For a gothic fantasy feel, this crafting adventure game puts you in the role of a witch. Explore the countryside, gather ingredients, and brew spells. A Redditor fondly recalls a ritual of playing it at a cafe on Saturday mornings. Stardew Valley : A quintessential cozy game, this farming simulator involves tending your farm, caring for animals, fishing, and undertaking quests. Its “cozy and impeccable vibes” and achievable goals provide a satisfying sense of accomplishment, akin to checking off a to-do list, according to a Reddit user. It’s important to remember that cozy gaming, while beneficial, is not a substitute for professional mental health care. Excessive gaming, generally considered 10 or more hours per week, can negatively impact work, sleep, and relationships. If your gaming habits interfere with daily life, it may be time to scale back.
Ultimately, the goal of cozy gaming is to leave you feeling better. “The activities should be fun, low-stress, and soothing to the nervous system, allowing you to breathe more deeply and recharge your batteries,” Dr. Kennedy advises. And with that sentiment, I’m ready to pick up the controller.
